summary: Validation of the Marketing Overview demo page: four components covering leads totals, leads-this-month volatility, Meta platform-vs-CRM daily comparison, and spend-by-campaign. Three defects found: a hidden visual filter on the leads bar chart, a misleading month-to-date card on stale data, and a campaign name source mismatch between the bar chart and table.

scope.period: Baseline 1-13 July 2026; full history explored for statistical probes
scope.data_completeness: Import watermark: inquiries through 2026-09-03, spend/Meta through 2026-09-04
scope.population: All franchises, all channels, no slicer pre-selections
scope.powerbi_identity: sample-dashboard.pbix on port 64741, catalog 7adfff38-1c62-4001-b51f-7fe7a396c9a4, verified by PBIDesktop pid 50356 window title and pbi.py capture

powerbi_risks.evidence: DAX definition uses TODAY() which drifts with machine clock on stale import
powerbi_risks.planned_experiment: Observed: card shows 535 for September but data ends Sept 3

powerbi_risks.evidence: Bar chart excludes Google Ads; spend chart includes only 6 campaigns
Bar chart reads dim_campaign, table reads fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily

claims.question: The "Date flag driven by the clock" check flagged 2 objects in this report. Is that intended here?
claims.expected: Date flags derived from the clock reflect the imported data's completeness, not the machine date.
claims.observed:
2 object(s). A calculated column is evaluated when the model is processed or recalculated, not when a visual queries it; a TODAY()/NOW() column freezes the clock at refresh time and can also be re-evaluated on open, so flags such as "completed month" drift away from the imported data. Hits: dim_date[is_completed_month_this_year]: dim_date[year] = YEAR ( TODAY () )
    && dim_date[date_key] < DATE ( YEAR ( TODAY () ), MONTH ( TODAY () ), 1 ); dim_date[is_current_month]: AND (
    YEAR ( dim_date[date_key] ) = YEAR ( TODAY () ),
    MONTH ( dim_date[date_key] ) = MONTH ( TODAY () )
)
claims.source: Model lint lint.volatile_time_in_column (severity high); agent explanation pending.

claims.expected: An imported snapshot ending 3 September 2026 should show the card is only counting leads from September 1-3, not the full month.
claims.observed: The card says 535 leads 'this month'. Today is September 18, but the data import watermark is September 3. The measure uses TODAY() = September 18 to select September, but only 3 days of September have data. The card shows 535 without indicating it covers only 3 out of 18 days. 27 days in September have no loaded data.
claims.source: Observed implementation, verified controls and current DAX; business approval pending.
claims.question: The card says 'Leads this month' but the data only goes through September 3. Does 535 represent 3 days or the full month? There is no label warning that most of the month is missing.

claims.expected: The CRM-attributed Meta leads should never exceed the platform-reported leads on any day (ratio should be at most 1.0).
claims.observed: The ratio exceeded 1.0 on 22 days across the full history. The worst cases: June 26 (CRM 109 vs Platform 23, ratio 4.7), August 11 (CRM 404 vs Platform 105, ratio 3.8), July 7 (CRM 133 vs Platform 60, ratio 2.2). On those days the CRM recorded far more Meta leads than the platform reported. This could mean leads are attributed to Meta in the CRM that Meta did not count, or there is a timing lag between systems.
claims.source: Observed implementation, verified controls and current DAX; business approval pending.
claims.question: On some days the CRM says Meta brought more leads than Meta itself reported. On June 26 the CRM counted 109 but the platform only 23. Is the CRM attributing leads to Meta that came from somewhere else?

claims.expected: Daily platform-reported Meta leads should follow a stable weekday pattern without extreme outliers.
claims.observed: August 11 (Tuesday) showed 105 platform-reported leads against a Tuesday median of 44, a z-score of 3.92. This is a strong outlier that warrants investigation.
claims.source: Observed implementation, verified controls and current DAX; business approval pending.
claims.question: August 11 had more than double the usual Tuesday volume from Meta. Was there a special campaign running, or is this a data anomaly?

claims.expected: The daily platform-reported Meta lead volume should be stable across the history.
claims.observed: A structural shift was detected around March 20: the median daily volume jumped from 1 to 41 leads. This likely reflects the launch of a Meta advertising campaign rather than a data error.
claims.source: Observed implementation, verified controls and current DAX; business approval pending.
claims.question: Before late March, Meta reported almost no daily leads; after that it jumped to about 40 per day. Is that when the Meta campaign started?

claims.expected: The bar chart and the table should list campaigns from the same source.
claims.observed: The bar chart uses campaign names from dim_campaign (a dimension table with 1004 more names than the fact table). The table uses campaign names directly from fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily. These are different columns from different tables. Additionally, the bar chart has a visual filter that includes only 6 specific campaigns while the table shows all. The bar chart total (sum of 6 campaigns) will not match the table's grand total.
claims.source: Observed implementation, verified controls and current DAX; business approval pending.
claims.question: The bar chart picks campaign names from a separate lookup table and shows only 6 of them. The table lists campaigns from the spend records directly and shows all of them. Their totals will not match. Is this the intended design?

findings.title: The bar chart lists campaigns from a dimension table while the table lists them from the spend fact table. Do these two sources agree on how many campaigns exist?
findings.explanation: Probe dax.assert failed: Observed 1004 == expected 0: does not hold.
findings.impact: Stated invariant does not hold in the imported population; the affected visuals inherit the error.

limitations: The Total Spend card showed abbreviated text (null parse) in all captures; its exact value was not verified against an oracle.
The 'Leads by channel' bar chart could not be captured separately from the table because both share the same title; the bar chart's marks were not independently parsed.

The Cost per Lead card uses DIVIDE([Aggregated Spend], [Contacts]) not DIVIDE([Spend], [Leads]); the denominator is contacts from fact_contact, not leads from fact_program_inquiry. This was noted but not tested as a separate component.
Channel slicer dropdown virtualization prevented testing toggle_member for Meta; Google Ads was used instead.

components.name: Total leads and leads by channel
components.definition: The Total Leads card and Leads (selected period) card both display the [Leads] measure (COUNTROWS of inquiries). The bar chart titled 'Leads by channel' has a visual-level filter that excludes Google Ads, so it shows fewer channels than the table with the same title, which has no filter. Both respond to the date slicer.

scenarios.description: Baseline: date range 1-13 July 2026, all channels selected. Shows the total leads count, bar chart of leads by channel (note: bar chart excludes Google Ads via a visual filter), and the channel table with all channels. Observed: Total Leads 4,360; Leads (selected period) 4,360; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $240K; Cost per Lead 74.29; leads total 4,360; 7/1/2026 to 7/13/2026.

Date range narrowed to 1-7 July 2026 only. The Total Leads and Leads (selected period) cards should drop because fewer days are included. The channel table total should still equal the card. Observed: Total Leads 2,252; Leads (selected period) 2,252; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $125K; Cost per Lead 74.62; leads total 2,252; 7/1/2026 to 7/7/2026.

Date range restored to 1-13 July 2026. All numbers should return to their baseline values, confirming the slicer drives these visuals. Observed: Total Leads 4,360; Leads (selected period) 4,360; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $240K; Cost per Lead 74.29; leads total 4,360; 7/1/2026 to 7/13/2026.

components.what_it_shows: How many prospective student inquiries came in during the selected date range, broken down by the marketing channel that brought them.

components.name: Leads this month
components.definition: The 'Leads this month' card displays the [Leads MTD] measure, which uses CALCULATE with FILTER(ALL(dim_date), month=MONTH(TODAY()) && year=YEAR(TODAY())). This overrides ALL date filters with the machine clock's current month. The label below says 'month to date'.

scenarios.description: Baseline: date range 1-13 July 2026. The 'Leads this month' card uses TODAY() to decide the current month, so it ignores the date slicer and always shows leads for the current calendar month (September 2026 as of today). The Total Leads and Leads (selected period) cards respond to the slicer. Observed: Total Leads 4,360; Leads (selected period) 4,360; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $240K; Cost per Lead 74.29; 7/1/2026 to 7/13/2026.

Date slicer moved to August 2026. The 'Leads this month' card should remain unchanged because it always reads the current month from the machine clock, not the slicer. The Total Leads and Leads (selected period) cards should change to reflect August inquiries. Observed: Total Leads 6,386; Leads (selected period) 6,386; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $381K; Cost per Lead 77.93; 8/1/2026 to 8/31/2026.

Date slicer restored to 1-13 July 2026. The 'Leads this month' card stays put, confirming it is independent of the date slicer. Total Leads and Leads (selected period) return to their baseline values. Observed: Total Leads 4,360; Leads (selected period) 4,360; Leads this month 535; Total Spend $240K; Cost per Lead 74.29; 7/1/2026 to 7/13/2026.

components.what_it_shows: How many prospective student inquiries arrived so far in the current calendar month, regardless of which date range you select on the page.

components.name: Meta leads, platform against CRM
components.definition: The line chart 'Meta leads: platform vs CRM by day' shows [Meta Direct Leads] (SUM of fact_meta_leads_daily[leads_onsite_grouped]) as 'Platform reported' and [Meta CL Leads] (CALCULATE([Leads], dim_channel[channel_key]="meta")) as 'CRM attributed'. The bar chart 'Meta lead match rate by day' shows [% Meta vs CL Leads] = DIVIDE([Meta CL Leads], [Meta Direct Leads]).

scenarios.description: Baseline: date range 1-13 July 2026. The 'Meta leads: platform vs CRM by day' line chart shows two lines: platform-reported leads from the ad platform export and CRM-attributed leads from inquiries tagged as Meta. The 'Meta lead match rate by day' bar chart shows the ratio (CRM / Platform) as a percentage. Observed: Total Leads 4,360; Leads (selected period) 4,360; Leads this month 535; 7/1/2026 to 7/13/2026.

components.name: Spend by campaign
components.definition: The bar chart 'Spend by campaign' uses dim_campaign[campaign_name] as the category axis and SUM(fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[spend]) as the value, with a visual filter limiting it to 6 specific campaigns. The table 'Spend by campaign' uses fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[campaign_name] directly (not the dimension table) and SUM(spend) with no visual filter.

scenarios.description: Baseline: date range 1-13 July 2026, all channels. The 'Spend by campaign' bar chart is filtered to 6 specific campaigns via a visual filter. The 'Spend by campaign' table has no visual filter and shows all campaigns. Compare whether these two agree on the campaigns shown and their spend totals.
